bundle.author: swain
bundle.title: Leave in-flight campaigns out of the plan-backfill cohort
bundle.body:
The backfill route selects campaigns without both plan sections persisted and processes them newest first. That set includes the campaigns the previous batch dispatched minutes earlier, so a call made while that batch is still generating re-selects exactly those campaigns. The service's in-flight check means nothing is dispatched and nothing is spent, but the call advances nothing and reports every one of them as dispatched. On prod today, batch three re-touched batch two's fifty and the operator had to notice from the unchanged eligible count.

A campaign whose linked run is queued, running or paused is now left out of the cohort, so repeated calls walk the backlog the way the doc already claimed. A failed run is not in flight: that campaign is still half-finished and still picked up, which is the recovery path the attempt cap exists for.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Scoped to admin backfill candidate SQL and docs; behavior is additive filtering with tests, no change to generation or auth paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Plan backfill cohort selection** now excludes campaigns that already have an in-flight plan generation run, so repeated admin backfill calls advance through the backlog instead of re-listing the same batch.
> 
> `selectCandidates` adds a `NOT EXISTS` check on `experiment_run` for runs linked via `campaign_strategy` opposition/opportunities run IDs when status is `QUEUED`, `RUNNING`, or `AWAITING_RESUME`. **Failed** runs are still eligible so half-finished plans can be retried. Tests cover skip vs select for those statuses; `AGENTS.md` documents the behavior for operators.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1fc2421acbe21c6fe0c3322c162add9e79bbb35a. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

priorFindings.body:
The `NOT EXISTS` clause excludes `QUEUED`, `RUNNING`, and `AWAITING_RESUME` but omits `SUPERSEDED`. In `campaignStrategy.service.ts`, `sectionState()` (line 537) explicitly treats `SUPERSEDED` as `'inflight'` — a SUPERSEDED run means a live successor was dispatched and may still be running. When `dispatchPending` sees both sections as `'inflight'` it skips dispatch and returns `{ status: 'generating' }`. The backfill's `run()` method only branches on `res.status === 'failed'`, so `'generating'` falls through to `outcomes.dispatched += 1` — the batch slot is consumed but no generation was actually started. This is the same wasted-call behaviour the PR set out to fix.

(Falsification check: no other guard exists — the SQL filter is the only place that prevents in-flight campaigns from being selected, and `sectionState()` is confirmed to return `'inflight'` for SUPERSEDED at line 537 of `campaignStrategy.service.ts`.)

The parameterized test covers `QUEUED`, `RUNNING`, and `AWAITING_RESUME` but omits `SUPERSEDED`. Since `sectionState()` in `campaignStrategy.service.ts` (line 537) classifies `SUPERSEDED` as in-flight and the comment says it 'should not be re-dispatched', a test case for this status would catch the missing filter value in the SQL and guard against regressions.

(Falsification check: the SQL at line 113 would need to already contain `'SUPERSEDED'` for this gap to be harmless; it does not.)

output.summary: The PR adds a NOT EXISTS subquery to the backfill candidate SQL that excludes campaigns with in-flight experiment runs (QUEUED, RUNNING, AWAITING_RESUME, SUPERSEDED), so repeated admin backfill calls advance through the backlog instead of re-selecting the same batch. The scout flagged a potential gap around COMPLETED runs within the 5-minute persist grace window, but deep review falsified this: the service-level sectionState() check already prevents double-dispatch for recently-completed runs, and campaigns with persisted sections are already excluded by the existing persisted_at IS NULL filter. The two prior findings about missing SUPERSEDED have been addressed — SUPERSEDED is now in both the SQL filter and the parameterized test. Tests cover all four excluded statuses plus a positive case for FAILED. The AGENTS.md documentation update accurately reflects the new behavior. Human reviewer should confirm the backfill route behaves as expected on the next operator run.
